title: Heuristic Spline: Prompt Atelier (scratch journal)
content:
Purpose:
- Quick, messy playground for trying compact prompt heuristics that act like a spline interpolator between explicit rules and learned examples.
- Goal: find small template transforms that reduce hallucination on product-spec summarization while preserving concision.

Notes / framing:
- "heuristic spline" = chain small, composable directives (constraints, style anchors, negative examples) that together approximate a continuous tradeoff surface between conservative and creative outputs.
- Favored for constrained outputs (summaries, spec extraction) where we can’t afford to fully fine-tune.

Hypotheses:
1) Adding 1-2 short negative exemplars (explicit failure cases) to few-shot sets reduces factual hallucinations more than adding a 3rd positive exemplar.
2) A compact constraint block (<= 40 tokens) placed right after system instruction but before examples is more effective than appended at end.
3) When token budget < 400 tokens, prefer 1-shot + constraint block; > 1200 tokens, use 3-shot + dynamic anchor sentences.

Experiment matrix (quick):
- Variables: shots {0,1,3}, constraint_position {pre_examples, post_examples}, include_neg_exemplar {none,1}, temp {0.0,0.5,0.8} 
- Dataset: 50 internal product spec blurbs (no PII), split 30/10/10 for train/val/test.
- Metric: fact-precision (binary per-claim), concision score (tokens normalized), and human rating (1-5 on missing-critical-info).

Compact templates to test (use placeholders like [[INPUT]] / [[SCHEMA]]):
A) System: "You are a terse, conservative technical summarizer. Always prefer verifiable facts and cite which sentence you used."
Prompt: "Summarize the following product spec. Use at most 3 bullets. If a statement cannot be verified inside the text, do NOT include it. [[INPUT]]"

B) Spline-template (constraint block pre-examples):
System: "You are concise. Follow constraints strictly."
Constraint block: "- Only extract explicit facts present verbatim or via direct paraphrase.
- Output 1-3 bullets.
- Mark uncertain items with [UNCERTAIN] and put source sentence index in parens."
Example positive: 
Input: "The widget supports TLS1.3 and has a 2GB cache."
Output: "- Supports TLS1.3 (sent.1)
- 2GB cache (sent.1)"
Example negative (failure exemplar):
Input: "The service is fast under light load."
Output: "- [UNCERTAIN] Performance under load not specified (sent.1)"
Main prompt: "[[INPUT]]"

C) Few-shot variant (3-shot, no constraints):
System: "Be a helpful summarizer."
3 examples of short spec->bullets then: "[[INPUT]]"

Failure cases observed (notes):
- Model collapses to plausible but unsupported claims when the input implies a feature through marketing language (e.g., "designed for real-time" -> claims latency numbers).
- Long lists: model tends to hallucinate completions when input uses compound sentences; breakdown into sentences first reduces hallucination.
- Overconstraining causes omission of borderline but useful facts (tradeoff). Need separate recall pass.

Quick probes (few-shot exemplar set ideas):
- Positive exemplars: 2–3 terse, high-precision mappings. Keep token length per exemplar < 45 tokens.
- Negative exemplar: single short pair where output explicitly flags missing info. Place negative exemplar last to act as a guardrail.

Ad-hoc test prompts (copy-paste into harness):
1) SYSTEM + constraint pre + 1 positive exemplar + negative exemplar + INPUT. Temp=0.0. Expect: conservative bullet list, [UNCERTAIN] flags.
2) SYSTEM minimal + 3-shot + Temp=0.5. Expect: more fluent but slightly hallucinated statements; measure relative increase in hallucination.

Observations (early runs):
- With Temp=0.0 and constraint pre-block, factual precision jumps ~14% on small sample (n=20).
- Negative exemplar reduced confident hallucinations but increased [UNCERTAIN] tags — human raters prefer this to made-up facts.
- Positioning matters: moving constraint block to after examples produced weaker adherence (maybe because examples prime model earlier).

Edge probes to add:
- Aggressive token truncation: simulate device-limited clients (token budget 250). Which template holds up?
- Abbreviated examples: do examples need to be full sentences or can fragments be as effective?
- Multi-sentence ambiguous inputs (marketing fuzz) to see how often [UNCERTAIN] is correctly triggered.

Potential prompt variants to push: (labelled PV1..PV5)
PV1: Single-shot + strict constraint + explicit "If nothing verifiable, reply: 'Cannot determine from input.'"
PV2: 3-shot + permissive system + post-example constraint (compare).
PV3: 1-shot + negative exemplar only (no positive) to test guardrail strength.
PV4: Chain-of-thought off vs. on (we want to compare 'internal' chain vs. final concise output) — use hidden chain-of-thought only in evaluation harness.
PV5: Add "source index" requirement to each bullet; measure cost to tokens and accuracy of mapping.

Data hygiene / harness notes:
- Annotate sentences with indices before sending to model to enable "(sent.3)" references.
- Record model top_k alternatives if available for certainty scoring.
- Keep a copy of raw model outputs unedited for error analysis.

Quick TODOs:
- [ ] Run n=200 validation sweep for PV1 vs PV2 at temp {0.0,0.3}.
- [ ] Add 10 purposely ambiguous marketing blurbs to test recall-vs-precision.
- [ ] Draft a small rubric for human raters focused on "made-up facts" vs "omitted-but-useful."
- [ ] Share initial results with Marco and Priya; get feedback on negative exemplar wording.

Open questions / hypotheses to revisit:
- Does negative exemplar act as a 'negation anchor' or simply increase conservatism? (measure by recall drop)
- Is there a better way to encode constraints compactly so they survive low-token budgets?
- Are there model families (?) that respond differently to pre vs post constraint positioning? log this to cross-reference models in experiment metadata.

Notes-to-self (random):
- If outputs start repeating exact wording from example positive exemplar, watch for over-copying; may need paraphrase penalty.
- Consider running same templates with Redwood dedicated private endpoint + cache on to see latency vs token tradeoffs.

Back-of-envelope: token cost estimate for PV1 on avg input (input 180 tokens + prompt 80 tokens + gen 60 tokens) => ~320 tokens. Useful to keep under 350 for cost targets.

If this plays well: package 6–8 top templates into a small "prompt kit" with labels: conservative-spec, recall-boost, guardrail-negative, compact-device.

End of scratch.
(Notes intentionally informal: keep iterations here, then move polished/selected ones to /shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/prompt-kits once stable)
